title: Philippines' Secretary Calls Maritime Law a Global Shield in Wake of 10th Anniversary of 2016 South China Sea Award
text: Philippines' Secretary Calls Maritime Law a Global Shield in Wake of 10th Anniversary of 2016 South China Sea Award Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro addressed European diplomats at Manila's 17th Festival della Diplomazia, emphasizing the 2016 South China Sea arbitration award's enduring validity and the need for ASEAN to adopt a binding maritime code of conduct while addressing the Myanmar crisis. The Philippines' foreign minister, Secretary Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro, delivered a prominent speech at the 17th Festival della Diplomazia in Manila on October 26, 2026, urging global leaders to recognize the growing importance of maritime security in the Indo‑Pacific. She framed the dialogue around the 10th anniversary of the 2016 South China Sea arbitral award, which effectively invalidated China's extensive claims in the contested waters under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. The award, she explained, remains a decisive, binding legal outcome that provides protection for smaller countries against dominant powers, underscoring the role of international law as a safeguard for sovereign rights.Lazaro Warns Of Erosion Of International LawDuring her address, Lazaro highlighted the Philippine government's consistent diplomatic restraint in the face of ongoing coercion and intimidation from Beijing in the South China Sea, stressing that restraint does not equal capitulation. She warned European policymakers that neglecting violations in Asian waters would erode the authority of international law worldwide, noting that a weakened stance in the Philippines would inevitably ripple out to other maritime hotspots such as the Mediterranean and Adriatic seas.\"The Philippines seeks no confrontation. Neither do we relinquish our lawful rights,\" she affirmed.In addition, the secretary outlined Manila's strategic roadmap for its ASEAN Chairmanship in 2026. She urged the Southeast Asian bloc to transition from ceremonial commemorations to tangible, enforceable solutions, specifically calling for a legally binding code of conduct in the South China Sea that honors the UNCLOS framework. Lazaro also stressed the importance of a comprehensive response to the Myanmar crisis, describing it as an inclusive process that engages all regional actors.Philippines Urges Legally Binding Code Of ConductHer theme, \"Navigating Our Future, Together,\" signaled a commitment to multilateral cooperation and to strengthening collective maritime resilience across the Indo‑Pacific region.
summary: Philippines' Secretary Calls Maritime Law a Global Shield in Wake of 10th Anniversary of 2016 South China Sea Award Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro, delivered a prominent speech at the 17th Festival della Diplomazia in Manila on October 26, 2026, urging global leaders to recognize the growing importance of maritime security in the Indo‑Pacific.
